output:
Short answer: pick an adjustable LED task lamp with high efficacy (integrated LED, dimmable, adjustable head/arm, 2700–5000 K options) — from your catalog the Meadowlight Lamp is a good candidate. If you want one specific recommendation now, I can pull the Meadowlight’s full specs/price and compare it to two alternatives.

Why an adjustable LED task lamp
- LEDs use far less power than incandescent/halogen for the same light output (typical: 8–15 W LED ≈ 60 W incandescent equivalent).
- Dimming + adjustable beam lets you use only the light you need, reducing energy use.
- Tunable color temperature (warm to cool) improves visual comfort for different tasks and times of day, reducing eye strain.
- Look for high efficacy (lumens per watt), CRI ≥ 80–90 for color accuracy, and ENERGY STAR or similar certification when possible.

What I found in your catalog memory
- “Meadowlight Lamp” (catalog entry)
- Generic entries: “adjustable desk lamps,” “desk lamp,” “task lamps,” “lighting products”
Evidence available: only the presence/names of these catalog items were returned. There are no product spec sheets or verified wattage/ lumen/CRI/ENERGY STAR details in the returned memory results.

Claims that require verification before purchase
- Actual power draw (watts) and lumen output
- Lumens per watt (efficacy)
- Color temperature range (K) and whether it’s tunable
- CRI (color rendering index)
- Dimming type and range (smooth, steps, PWM)
- ENERGY STAR or other efficiency certifications
- Warranty, expected lifetime (hours), and replacement policy
- Price and stock/lead time
- Mounting options (base, clamp) and adjustability specs

Example energy-savings estimate (illustrative)
- Assumptions: 8 hours/day, 5 days/week, 50 weeks/year, electricity $0.15/kWh
- 60 W incandescent → annual energy = 60 W × 8 × 5 × 50 = 120,000 Wh = 120 kWh → cost ≈ $18.00/yr
- 10 W LED → annual energy = 10 W × 8 × 5 × 50 = 20 kWh → cost ≈ $3.00/yr
- Estimated saving ≈ $15/yr per lamp (plus lower heat and bulb replacement costs).
(These numbers are examples — actual savings depend on the lamp’s true wattage and usage.)

What I recommend next
1. Tell me your priorities (budget, desk size, clamp vs base, need for USB/PD, smart-home integration, preferred color temp, number of lamps).
2. If you want, I will fetch full specs, certifications, price and availability for the Meadowlight Lamp and compare it with two other high-efficacy desk lamps from the catalog so you can pick the best energy-efficient option.

Which would you like me to do next?
